summary: Backend testing for People Ops employee schedules & days-off (iteration 219). Wrote 21 pytest tests covering all new endpoints + regressions. All 21 tests passed.
coverage: POST /schedules/employee/{id} creates with weekly_pattern (7 days), auto weekly_hours_total=40, threshold default supported
Second POST supersedes v1: status='superseded', effective_to=(new_from - 1 day)=2026-02-28
PUT on active updates pattern and recomputes weekly_hours_total
expected-hours: 7 daily entries, Sunday=0 when pattern.sunday.work_hours=0, sum equals total_hours
expected-hours: date before any schedule returns 0
days-off create, duplicate 400, list-in-range, delete success/404
team-calendar returns {start_date, end_date, events[], employees[]} with valid event types
critical_code_review_comments: team_calendar calls compute_expected_hours() per-employee inside a loop — O(N employees) DB roundtrips. For orgs with many employees over a wide date range this may be slow. Consider batching schedule/days-off queries once and computing in-memory.
team_calendar filter uses status {$ne: 'terminated'} for employees; ensure this aligns with your active-employee semantics (some codebases use status='active' explicitly).
DELETE /schedules/{id} has a docstring implying it should refuse deletion if used in payroll/OT, but no such check exists in code — either implement or update docstring.

create_employee_schedule supersedes prior versions only when effective_from is later; a POST with an earlier or same effective_from as an existing active version could create overlapping active versions. Consider validating monotonic effective_from or handling backward-dated inserts explicitly.
seed_data_creation: Test schedules and days-off created and cleaned up in the test lifecycle (uses TEST_ prefix in notes/reason).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All schedule/days-off endpoints verified. Legacy overtime/time-off regressions still green. Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_people_ops_schedules.py is fully idempotent and can be re-run standalone.
